mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the uniqueness constraint on (forApp, eventType, actor) triples allows the model to create two ApplicationEvents that share the same application+eventType+actor, representing an in-place mutation/replacement. The AppendOnly predicate detects this via the 'no two distinct events share the same triple' clause, which will then find a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: ApplicationEvent | e1.forApp = e2.forApp and e1.eventType = e2.eventType and e1.actor = e2.actor }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the at-most-one-pending constraint allows the model to construct two LoanApplications with the same owner both in PendingReview status. The FR_005_OnePendingPerCustomer predicate will find this as a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OnePendingViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.owner = a2.owner and a1.status = PendingReview and a2.status = PendingReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the LeastPrivilege enforcement fact allows the model to create an Operation where a Customer successfully calls OpPostDecision (outcome = OutSuccess), violating the permission matrix. The LeastPrivilege predicate's implication 'OutSuccess implies in Allowed' catches this.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = OpPostDecision and op.caller.role = Customer and op.outcome = OutSuccess }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the NoInformationLeakage fact allows the model to construct an Operation where a Customer calls GetAppByRef on another customer's application and receives OutDenied instead of OutNotFound, leaking existence information. The predicate checks for OutNotFound specifically.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeakageViolation { some op: Operation, u1, u2: User, a: LoanApplication | op.kind = OpGetAppByRef and op.caller = u1 and u1.role = Customer and op.targetApp = a and a.owner = u2 and u1 != u2 and op.outcome = OutDenied }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the fact that every decided application must have exactly one decision audit event allows the model to have an Approved application with no ApprovedEvt ApplicationEvent. The AuditCompleteness and FR_016_AuditTrailComplete predicates both check for the existence of that event and will find a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingDecisionEvent { some a: LoanApplication | a.status = Approved and (no e: ApplicationEvent | e.forApp = a and e.eventType = ApprovedEvt) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the at-most-one-decision constraint allows two distinct Decision records to point to the same LoanApplication, representing a race condition where two concurrent staff decisions both succeed. The ConcurrencySafety and FR_012_ConcurrentDecisionRejected predicates both enforce lone/no duplicate decisions per application.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateDecision { some disj d1, d2: Decision | d1.forApp = d2.forApp }
